gap: No result ChatGPT got states that, among the 16-inch 2560x1600 120 Hz-and-up portable screens, only the ASUS ZenScreen MB16QHG has a named brightness measurement (481 cd/m2 at Monitornerds, 417 cd/m2 at TechRadar Pro, against ASUS's 500 claim, with TechRadar Pro reporting a 60% brightness cap on a single USB-C cable), while UPERFECT's only measured sibling read 238 nits at Parkablogs.
standout_why: Compared against Macworld's Mac roundup (updated 2026-11-25) and PCWorld's roundup (2026-06-26), both opened. Macworld gives only spec-sheet figures (Duex Float 2 Pro: 350 nits, 100% sRGB, 2.9 lb) and does not cover the UPERFECT 16-inch, SOTSU, Arzopa or MB16QHG. PCWorld has three measured figures, all for screens outside the 16-inch 16:10 120 Hz line (ViewSonic VX1655-4K-OLED 457 nits, Arzopa Z1FC 337 nits, HP 514pn 1710:1). Neither has measured power draw or a measured-versus-claimed comparison for the line's candidates. Limit on this judgement: the RTINGS roundup and the TechRadar roundup would not load their body text (TechRadar showed only the MSI Pro MP165 E6 entry and an Arzopa Z3FC caption), so I could not check them.
decides: It does not move the pick by itself, but it changes how the brightness ranking must be worded. The UPERFECT GR16EQ's 450 cd/m2 and the Duex Float 2 Pro's 350 nits are maker claims that no named reviewer I could open has measured, so those rows should say whose figure it is. The one measured UPERFECT 16-inch 2560x1600 120 Hz screen (UPlays C2, Parkablogs, 2023) read 238 nits, so a lead that rests on 450 against 350 is a claimed lead only. The MB16QHG is the only candidate whose brightness lead holds up in measurement (417 to 481 cd/m2), but TechRadar Pro says one-cable use limits it to 60% brightness, and the desk notes have it out of stock at ASUS. The Float 2 Pro keeps the stacked-above-the-MacBook segment on layout, not on any measurement.
candidates: Arzopa Z3FC (ChatGPT's value pick; 16.1-inch 2560x1440, outside the 16:10 line)

findings.label: Measured peak brightness (Monitornerds)
findings.note: Paolo Reva, review dated 2023-08-04; instrument not named. Quote: "The Asus ZenScreen MB16QHG's backlight reached 481 cd/m2". The page's own spec list gives ASUS's 500 cd/m2, so the measurement is 19 cd/m2 under the claim.

findings.label: Measured contrast, gamut, color error and input lag (Monitornerds)
findings.value: 1504:1 at 50% brightness; 100% sRGB, 98% DCI-P3, 86% Adobe RGB; average deltaE 3.12 out of the box, 0.96 calibrated; input lag 6 ms at 120 Hz
findings.note: Paolo Reva, 2023-08-04; instrument not named. The page's spec list says 144 Hz while the body says 120 Hz. The 2.65 lb weight on the page is the spec figure, not a weighing.

findings.label: Measured brightness (TechRadar Pro)
findings.source_title: Hands on: I tried out the Asus ZenScreen MB16QHG (TechRadar Pro)
findings.note: Instrument not named. The page also gives 116% DCI-P3 and 163% sRGB, which read as gamut volume, not coverage. My read returned a date of 28 March 2025 and the byline Brandon Hill, but a search listing attributes the testing to PC Pro: re-check the byline before naming a person, and cite it as TechRadar Pro's review until then.

findings.label: Brightness limit on one USB-C cable (TechRadar Pro)
findings.value: 60% brightness on a single USB-C cable; 100% needs the included wall adapter
findings.source_title: Hands on: I tried out the Asus ZenScreen MB16QHG (TechRadar Pro)
findings.note: Quote: "Relying on a single USB-C cable to handle all the heavy lifting for power and video limits you to a 60% brightness." The review does not name the laptop used, so this is not a MacBook-specific result.

findings.product: UPERFECT UPlays C2 (16-inch 2560x1600 120 Hz; earlier model in the family the GR16DQ comes from)
findings.label: Measured max brightness and gamut (Parkablogs)
findings.value: 238 nits; 100% sRGB, 71% NTSC, 76% P3, 76% AdobeRGB after calibration
findings.source_title: Review: UPERFECT UPlays C2 portable gaming 16-inch display (Parkablogs)
findings.note: Teoh Yi Chie, 2023-06-20; instrument not named. Quote: "Measured max brightness of 238 nits is sufficient for use in a bright room environment." The review gives 720 g, the same net weight the desk notes carry for the GR16DQ (0.72 kg), but I did not confirm that the UPlays C2 and the GR16DQ share a panel. Treat it as a measurement of an older sibling, not of the GR16DQ or GR16EQ.

findings.label: Measured brightness and power draw by brightness setting (ServeTheHome)
findings.source_title: Arzopa Z3FC 16.1in 180Hz 2.5K Portable Monitor review, page 2 (ServeTheHome)
findings.note: Sam Sabinash, dated 2026-04-12; Datacolor SpyderPro; power measured at the USB-C power input. ServeTheHome cautions: "This is not the fanciest test equipment by any means". This is the only measured power draw I could source for any candidate: about 12 W at full brightness, which a bus-powered screen would take from the MacBook's port.

findings.note: Same review and instrument. The Z3FC is 2560x1440 at 180 Hz per PCWorld's roundup (16:9), so it sits outside the 16:10 2560x1600 line; it is here because ChatGPT made it the value pick.
